footnote: Consumer study: 97% subjects said skin felt less oily throughout the day after using this serum for 2 weeks. Frames are AI illustrations, not real results.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: a pure white seamless paper backdrop, soft daylight from the upper left, a faint grey contact-shadow area on the right. Square 1080x1080. Keep the right 45% of the frame as an empty space, evenly lit, for a pack photo placed later, and keep the left half as a calm empty area for copy. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, consented, unretouched photos of one person at day 1 and week 2 of the routine (same light and framing) to replace the AI frames.

caption: Salicylic Acid 2% Face Serum: apply 2-3 drops after cleansing & toning, in the PM. Start every alternate day; after 2 weeks, use it every day.

findings.span: 97% said skin felt less oily throughout the day
findings.message: The headline drops 'subjects' and has no asterisk, so '97%' can read as 97% of all users, and the 2-week duration appears only in the footnote. The perception wording ('said skin felt') is correctly kept.
findings.fix: 97% subjects said skin felt less oily throughout the day*, with the footnote opening '*Consumer study:' so the asterisk links the headline to its qualifier.

findings.message: A Day 1 to Week 2 frame pair beside a 97% headline reads as a before/after, and the footnote says the frames are AI illustrations, so the ad depicts a 2-week change nobody photographed; it also makes a self-reported 'felt less oily' look like a visible, measured result (CLM-08) and implies a timed result (CLM-07). The rulebook rates CLM-15 as fix; my view is that this must not run with these frames.
findings.fix: Use real, consented, unretouched photos from the 2-week study with the qualifier, or drop the Day 1 / Week 2 frames and pair the stat with a pack or texture shot; either way, 'Frames are AI illustrations, not real results.' then goes.

findings.message: A time-bound result needs a study of that duration, with the qualifier shown on the creative.
findings.fix: Keep the timeframe only if it comes from a study you can cite, and put the qualifier in the footnote (e.g. '*Consumer perception study, 4 weeks'). Otherwise remove the timeframe.
findings.note: Wording appears on the product page (F13). Severity lowered one step: the brand has published it, but a reviewer must still confirm substantiation is on file.

findings.message: Statistics need their study qualifier on the creative and must not be worded more strongly than the study.
findings.fix: Quote the stat exactly as the study states it ('90% subjects said…') and add a footnote: study type (consumer perception / in-vivo / in-vitro), duration, and n if known.
